item.title: The Taliban has taken a terrible toll on the education of girls -- and boys as well
item.description: Saturday marks the 5th anniversary of the current Taliban rule in Aghanistan. They've had a devastating impact on girls' education. A lesser told story is their impact on the education of boys.
item.content:encoded:

(Image credit: Mohsen Karimi/AFP)

item.title: Feds probe 'mention markets.' And, lawmakers call for investigation into USS Lincoln
item.description: Federal regulators are reviewing 'mention markets' that allow wagers on what public figures will say. And, Democratic lawmakers call for an investigation into conditions on the long-deployed USS Lincoln.

item.title: Sen. Ruben Gallego on handling of USS Lincoln conditions: 'That's not proper leadership'
item.description: Lawmakers want answers from the Pentagon chief and the U.S. Navy about living conditions aboard the USS Lincoln. NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Democratic Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona.

item.title: From Europe to Asia, floods to heatwaves, world experiences weather shocks
item.description: At least eight people died in Japan as heavy rains flooded roads and disrupted traffic while firefighters from Britain to France and Croatia struggled to contain blazes in Europe's fifth heatwave this summer

item.title: New aircraft carrier heads toward Mideast after reports of issues on long-deployed USS Lincoln

item.title: By sky and sea, Ukraine's drone strikes challenge Russia's grip on Crimea
item.description: Russia maintained an iron grip on Crimea since seizing it from Ukraine in 2014. Many Russian civilians go there to enjoy the beaches. But now Ukraine is hitting Crimea hard, upending daily life.
